body: The spec says `<q>My query</q>` instead of `"My query"` but not sure how to use tags in there.
Could be done in https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/5484c62e2fa29938305718efd82f0a585c8dde30/src/lib/utils.js#L227 but it'd be a huge refactor.
The label itself should stay `label`; it's the rendering that should add the `q`
Sure, it makes sense!
Rather than the `configure` widget could be nice to have the widgets directly. It let us play with the widget add / remove refinements - it's easier to test / understand how the widget works.

It should be `use excludedAttributes`. 

Worth adding an example that show how the previous implementation was working vs the current one.

Do we really have to provide the index? We can assume that for each refinement the 4-tuple is a unique identifier? It doesn't make sense to have two refinement with the exact same information. Did you have any issue without the index?
Do we really have to implement this hook? Did you notice any performance bottleneck?
We tried to be consistent with the naming so it would make more sense to have `items` rather than `refinements`. But I agree that `items[].item.items` feels a bit odd. Any ideas?

body: With a count of 0 the object won't be spread.
With a non exhaustive count the object won't be spread.
Why are we using `clearRefinements` rather than `removeHierarchicalFacetRefinement`? The latter avoid to drop other refinements in case there are some on the same attribute.
We can add a test case for this change since it's an issue on the current implementation.
